Thanks Stephan,

I applied the patch and it worked for me. The plotting seems to be a bit slow for large maps though. Simon, any chance of applying this to the package?

One additional note... The colors for raster images seem to be pretty washed out in JavaGD devices. here is an example:

library(OpenStreetMap)
lat <- c(43.834526782236814,30.334953881988564)
lon <- c(-131.0888671875 ,-107.8857421875)
southwest <- openmap(c(lat[1],lon[1]),c(lat[2],lon[2]),zoom=6,'osm')
#non-raster
plot(southwest)
#raster
plot(southwest,raster=TRUE)


the colors for the non-raster image matches those in other devices

best,
ian

messages.body_plain:
On Aug 8, 2012, at 4:31 AM, Julien Cochennec wrote:

> Looks like I got the answer for Question 1, Acinonyx is no Java, right? I found no Java code in the source.
> 

iPlots are written in Java, but iPlots eXtreme (aka Acinonyx) is not (for performance reasons).

On Aug 8, 2012, at 4:07 AM, Julien Cochennec wrote:

> Hi,
> Newbies to Iplots. We're developing a Java app here, it calls R to build charts, now we want to make interactive charts and Iplots looks perfect for that.

> 1) The Gui built by the "idev()" command is Java Gui, right?

It's not a GUI, it is simply an R graphics device embedded in iPlots. Note that for Java you get the same thing with the JavaGD package.


> 2) Is there a way to "plug it" into another Spring Gui by adding parameters to "idev(...)"?

Again, it's not a GUI, but you can combine multiple idevs (or even iplots) in one icontainer (see help page for the latter).


> 3) Is there a way to build listeners and event so our app can detect when changes append in the idev() Gui?


Since idev is just a regular R device, you can use the regular R device hooks.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Rserve - cannot connect
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to set up an R server on Ubuntu (precise) with R 2.15
installed. I want to connect from remote an my configuration file
/etc/Rserv.conf is set like this:

remote enable
auth disable
fileio enable
maxinbuf 500000

The telnet test works. But my application cannot connect
(createConnection() fails):

If I check the settings with --RS-settings, I get:

Rserve v0.6-8

config file: /etc/Rserv.conf
working root: /tmp/Rserv
port: 6311
local socket: [none, TCP/IP used]
authorization required: no
plain text password: not allowed
passwords file: [none]
allow I/O: yes
allow remote access: no
control commands: no
interactive: yes
max.input buffer size: 262144 kB

So remote access seems to be disabled though it should be enabled?

The configuration file was taken from an older installation (older
Ubuntu, R 2.12) and this Rserver is running well with my application.
What else could be the reason for my problem?

Antje

Yes, sorry, that is a historical oddity - in the beginning the project was called "Rserv" as can be seen in traces like the source file names and the config file name. Before it was released on CRAN it was changed to "Rserve" (inspired by Xserve at the time - funny that Rserve outlived Xserves :)) but the file names remained and now it's too late to change it ...

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: Strange JGR bug
messages.body_plain:
Dear Simon and Mark,

I have run into the same problem (JGR dropdown menus merely flashing for a
split-second, no chance to select) and found that even Firefox used to give its
users trouble with dropdown menus (albeit sometime back in version 4: compare
http://support.mozilla.org/de/questions/716983).  

There seems to be an issue with hardware acceleration. 
On my MacBook (running OS 10.6.8) I got rid of the "Application Enhancer", now I
am back to selecting the appropriate data sets.

Hope something along those lines works for you, too.

Christoph

ps: the problem seemed to first occur after I had put my computer to sleep with
JGR running; not sure what to make of that, though... might have caused
acceleration to be available/necessary in some way.
